audit.why: FAV at 4/10 matches a 58.14% Aurora win rate over 86 games: she owns levels 2 through first item and loses the two-item stage outright.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, and Spirit Fire is never mentioned at all despite being Nasus's only ranged tool in the lane.
audit.why: Wither is 15/14/13/12/11s at 700 range, Spirit Fire is a flat 12s at 650 range and shreds armour, Fury of the Sands is 120/100/80s. Those are the timings that make 'trade on his cooldown' actionable.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer states 'Wither is point-blank range, so at this distance he has no answer.' That is false and it is the single most dangerous line on the page. It also calls Wither a grounding effect in the late-game section, and nothing mentions that Siphoning Strike is an auto-attack reset or that Fury of the Sands deals percent-health damage.
audit.why: Riot's data gives Wither a range of 700 — further than Siphoning Strike (255) and Spirit Fire (650), and equal to Across the Veil's 700-unit leap. A player told it is point-blank will stand at 600 units and get Withered every time. Wither is a Move Speed and Attack Speed decay, not a grounding, so it does not stop your W or R. Fury of the Sands is percent-health magic damage and also grants him bonus Armor, Magic Resist and attack range while it runs.
audit.corrected: early now reads 'Wither reaches 700 units, so hold that gap'; late says 'craters your kiting'; report[5] carries the range and the percent-HP note; dontsFull[1] names the Siphoning Strike auto reset.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Aurora level 1 and only Skill at first item and two items, contradicting the packet chart and the prose.
audit.why: whys[0] calls level 1 a skill check, whys[5] calls first item Aurora's spike, and whys[6] says the two-item window is his. The packet chart on both the aurora and nasus packets reads Skill/Aurora/Aurora/Aurora/Aurora/Aurora/Nasus.
audit.corrected: Three tokens flipped as one atomic group in both layers, with phases[0].why and phases[6].why rewritten to match.

edits.before: Q-E weave stacks your passive drain from range. Identify how Nasus contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: You out-range him but have no escape until W, and he only wants to farm — so deny Siphoning Strike last-hits.

edits.before: Two items on: your pattern is at full power. Nasus carry threat 10/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Stacked Siphoning Strike plus a 700-range Wither one-shots you — close the game before this window arrives.

edits.before: His only kite. W-blink through it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: 700-range slow on 15s at rank 1. Stay outside it or W out once it lands.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Wither reaches 700 and Siphoning Strike is an auto reset — leave early.

edits.before: - Nasus Wither: matchup-defining — His only kite. W-blink through it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Wither: matchup-defining — 15s at rank 1 and 700 range, further than you think. - Spirit Fire: 12s, shreds your armour. - Across the Veil: 22s. - Between Worlds: kill windows only.

edits.before: Track Nasus's Wither: His only kite. W-blink through it. When it is down — Q-E + R him.
edits.after: Wither is a 700-range slow, not point-blank; his R burns percent HP, so resists do not help.

edits.before: Level 1 is roughly even — you are a single-target poke mage with no hard escape until W, and he only wants to last-hit, so stay at range, deny his Siphoning Strike (Q) stacks, and do not over-extend into a jungle gank. From level 2 the lane tilts to you: fire Twofold Hex (Q), recast it to pull the curse back through him for the second hit, then E (The Weirding) to slow him and hop backward so he eats poke he can't trade back — Wither is point-blank range, so at this distance he has no answer. Your passive spirits heal you through every exchange, so the longer the poke war runs the further ahead you get. Just hold W (Across the Veil) for the dodge — it is your only real escape if his jungler shows.

edits.before: Be honest — this flips. Nasus is a hard scaler, and once Siphoning Strike (Q) is stacked and he has Wither plus his R lifesteal and size online, he shrugs off your poke and a single Wither grounds your kiting long enough for a stacked Q to delete you. Your kit has no way to survive a fully-stacked Q connecting. So your entire job is to make late game never happen: snowball your early-mid lead into turret plates, roam off W mobility, and force objectives to end before the 2+ item mark. If it goes long, use R untargetability to reposition and let your team peel — never duel him.

notes: WIN RATE CONFLICT, not edited: tools/audit-run/packets/aurora.json reports 58.14% over 86 games for Aurora vs Nasus, but MC_WR_TABLES.aurora.nasus in champ-data/content/aurora.js says 53.69, and the nasus packet reports 46.31% for Nasus (= 53.69 for Aurora) over 434 games. The two packets disagree with each other. I left every win-rate number alone. The 434-game figure looks like the better sample. Champion-level issues also present here: 'Between the Worlds' in phases[4].why and breakdown.late should be 'Between Worlds', and dontsFull/tradeBad reuse the boilerplate 'you are a immobile drain bot' (missing 'an') across many Aurora matchups. Aurora kit flag misfires: her passive is flagged 'anti-heal target' when Riot's text says it heals HER, and her R is flagged hardCC when the description lists only damage and slows.
